newsitem.title: TURKEY: Key Turk Islamist MP denies resignation reports.
newsitem.headline: Key Turk Islamist MP denies resignation reports.

text.p: An Islamist MP close to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan denied press reports he could resign over government reluctance to comply with army orders to stamp out religious activism.
"I've come so far and I'll keep on going, given that there is not a very serious conflict of opinions at this point," Anatolian news agency quoted Aydin Menderes as saying on Wednesday night.
Menderes, from the liberal wing of Erbakan's pro-Islam Welfare Party, criticised the coalition 10 days ago for stalling on the military's demands. The Turkish media had said he could step down.
The secularist army has given Erbakan a list of 18 anti-Islamist measures it wants carried out, including restrictions on Islamist education, and enforcement of a ban on Islamic dress.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, met army chief Ismail Hakki Karadayi on Tuesday after a senior general said the fight against Islamist trends was a matter of life and death for Turkey.
Menderes, whose father Adnan was deposed as prime minister and executed after a 1960 coup, said Erbakan's relations with the army were improving.

"The meeting between Erbakan and Karadayi is important," Menderes said. "The government is trying to get over this bottleneck. The problems between the army and government cannot go on for ever," he said.
